query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: issue_domain
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the incident type from short_description, giving a strong grouping axis to compare resolution times across domains. Values (vpn, connectivity, database, email) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: severity_signal
per_column.rationale: A severity/symptom axis is genuinely useful for predicting resolution effort. However, mappings are sometimes strained: 'Cannot connect to database' -> access_denial and 'Email system not working properly' -> system_down are inferred beyond what the terse text clearly supports, so some values are weakly grounded.

per_column.name: resolution_path_complexity
per_column.rationale: Whether the closer differs from the resolver/assignee is a plausible proxy for hand-off complexity and relevant to resolution time. Derivable by comparing closed_by/assigned_to fields; NULL for open incidents is correct behaviour.

per_column.name: assignee_specialization
per_column.rationale: Values are just the assignee name, essentially a restatement of the existing assigned_to column rather than a derived specialization measure. Grounded but adds little new analytical leverage.

per_column.name: caller_profile
per_column.rationale: Bucketing callers by report frequency (single/occasional/repeat/system) is a reasonable derived axis from caller_id counts and could correlate with resolution difficulty. Grounded in aggregated caller_id data.

per_column.name: infrastructure_outage_indicator
per_column.rationale: A boolean outage flag could matter for resolution time, but it is skewed (416 true) and its assignment appears loose: routine VPN/email/database issues all flagged True, which overstates 'infrastructure outage' beyond the source text and risks being near-constant.

per_column.name: diagnostic_clarity
per_column.rationale: Whether the problem is clearly diagnosable is conceptually relevant to resolution time, but from terse descriptions the true/false judgment is largely inferred and hard to verify; all samples are False, suggesting a weakly grounded, near-constant flag.

judge.rationale: Most columns supply genuine new axes (issue_domain, severity_signal, resolution_path_complexity, caller_profile) relevant to predicting slower resolution. Weak spots: assignee_specialization merely restates assigned_to, and the two boolean flags (infrastructure_outage_indicator, diagnostic_clarity) are skewed and inferred beyond what the terse source text clearly warrants. Grounding is generally sound for extraction/aggregation columns but softer for the inferred severity and boolean columns.
